newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UBS CEO reaffirms asset management goals.
newsitem.headline: UBS CEO reaffirms asset management goals.

text.p: Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS) chief executive Mathis Cabiallavetta said he still believed that UBS will have to buy an existing business in order to meet a strategic goal of expanding in asset managment in the U.S.

Cabiallavetta told a meeting of the Swiss-American Chamber of Commerce that UBS, Switzerland's biggest bank, remained interested in U.S. asset management, as he had already outlined at the annual news conference on February 21.
"I expect that we will need to make an acquisition at some point in order to establish ourselves (in asset management)," he said.

Cabiallavetta said UBS has to establish a larger presence in U.S. asset management in order to remain a global financial player, because the U.S. market was the biggest and fastest-growing for this business.
"That is the way our strategy is laid out, and something will be done here. We will see how long it takes," Cabiallavetta said.
He declined to elaborate on the timing or potential targets for an acquisition in this business when queried by reporters after his speech.
At the February press briefing, Cabiallavetta already said that acquisitions were likely to be part of UBS's strategy to expand in asset management and also in private banking.

On Monday, UBS provided a breakdown of its results by divisions showing that its private banking and institutional asset management divison, with a pre-tax income of 1.91 billion Swiss francs, was the largest contributor to earnings "by a wide margin." The figure was based on 1.63 billion from private banking, and 280 million from institutional asset management.
